reports.title: Patterson-UTI Energy Reports Financial Results for the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: In Drilling Services, we expect to operate an average of approximately 104 rigs in the United States during the fourth quarter and exit 2026 above that level, with additional rig reactivations anticipated in the first quarter of 2027. Results should benefit from continued pricing momentum, including higher dayrates across all rig classes and the deployment of upgraded rigs at dayrates above our current average. We expect to incur reactivation costs during the quarter as we prepare additional rigs for reactivation late in the fourth quarter and in early 2027, and we anticipate additional costs as we wind-down our operations in Colombia. Overall, we expect Drilling Services adjusted gross profit of $150 million in the fourth quarter.

In Completion Services, we expect fourth quarter adjusted gross profit of $140 million, supported by activity levels broadly consistent with the third quarter and additional pricing improvements. We anticipate some seasonal and holiday impact in the fourth quarter, although at this time it appears likely that it will be less pronounced than in prior fourth quarters. As we deploy new Emerald 100% natural gas powered equipment, we will continue to decommission diesel-powered assets and therefore do not expect active horsepower to increase through the first half of 2027.

In Drilling Products, we expect fourth quarter adjusted gross profit to decline 5-10%, sequentially, primarily reflecting the expectation for lower drilling activity in Saudi Arabia due to ongoing geopolitical unrest in the region.
We expect Other adjusted gross profit in the fourth quarter to be steady compared to the third quarter.

For the fourth quarter, we expect general and administrative expense to be approximately $70 million and depreciation, depletion, amortization, and impairment expense to be approximately $220 million.
Except for cash dividends per common share, all references to “per share” in this press release are diluted earnings per common share as defined within Accounting Standards Codification Topic 260.
